question: What does the acronym IEC stand for in public health?
explanation: IEC is a core public health strategy that stands for Information, Education, and Communication, used to guide community health promotion. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h1)

question: Why is communication considered a two-way process in the IEC framework?

options.A: It focuses only on passing medical news from the hospital to the village
options.B: It requires two different nurses to speak at the same community meeting
options.C: It means printing health materials in both English and a local language
options.D: It involves listening to community feedback and addressing local fears

explanation: Effective communication in IEC goes beyond just giving orders; it requires listening to what the community has to say and clearing up doubts. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h1)

question: At which stage of behavior change is a person not yet thinking about changing because they see no problem?
explanation: Think of precontemplation as 'before thinking about it.' The person isn't worried about their habit yet, so change isn't on their mind at all! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h2)

question: A patient knows her diet is unhealthy and plans to start eating vegetables next week, but hasn't bought any yet. Which stage is she in?
explanation: She is getting ready to make a change very soon (like planning for next week), which puts her right in the preparation stage. You've got this! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h2)

question: According to the Health Belief Model, what must a person feel before taking health action?

options.A: Vulnerable to the disease and aware of its seriousness
options.B: Fully trained to treat others with the same condition
options.C: Required by local law to report to a health facility
options.D: Financially compensated for visiting the local clinic

explanation: People only change their health habits when they realize, 'This sickness can actually affect me, and it is quite serious!' That's the heart of the Health Belief Model. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h3)

question: Why do nurses study behavioral theories like the Health Belief Model in primary health care?

options.A: To calculate the precise drug dosage for chronic illnesses
options.B: To accurately diagnose complex internal organ diseases
options.C: To understand why people do or do not adopt healthy practices
options.D: To replace laboratory tests with patient interviews

explanation: Behavioral theories help us look beyond simple medical orders and truly understand the human side of why patients make certain health choices. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h3)

question: In health education, what do we call the path or medium used to carry a message to the community?
explanation: Think of a 'channel' like a TV channel or a road—it's the route or tool (like radio, posters, or town criers) that carries the message from you to the community. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h4)

question: Why is it best to combine mass media with face-to-face counselling in health campaigns?

options.A: Mass media is always more accurate than anything a nurse can say in person
options.B: Government regulations require both methods to be used simultaneously
options.C: Face-to-face counselling is too expensive to use unless mass media has failed
options.D: Mass media reaches many people quickly, while face-to-face counselling allows personal questions

explanation: Radio and posters help spread the word far and wide fast, but sitting down to talk allows patients to ask questions and clear up personal doubts! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h4)

question: What is most important when creating health education posters for a rural Nigerian community?

options.A: Ensuring every poster costs very little to print
options.B: Writing the text exclusively in advanced medical English
options.C: Featuring foreign medical experts on the cover page
options.D: Using local languages and familiar cultural imagery

explanation: For health messages to stick, people need to see themselves in the pictures and understand the language without struggling. Keep it relatable! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h5)

question: Why should nurses involve traditional and religious leaders when starting a new community health project?

options.A: They provide free medical supplies to the clinic
options.B: Their approval builds trust and community acceptance
options.C: They are trained to audit hospital financial records
options.D: They write all official government health policies

explanation: Community leaders hold great influence. When they support a health initiative, the people are much more willing to listen and participate. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h5)

question: As an IEC implementer in a community clinic, what is one of the nurse's main jobs?

options.A: Educating patients during routine care and outreach sessions
options.B: Constructing physical buildings for the local health center
options.D: Enforcing legal penalties for ignoring health advice

explanation: Everyday clinic visits, immunizations, and community outreaches are golden opportunities for nurses to teach and counsel patients. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h6)

question: A mother at an immunization clinic says she is scared a vaccine causes infertility. How should the nurse respond?

options.A: Ignore the comment and administer the injection without saying a word
options.B: Scold the patient for listening to unverified neighborhood rumors
options.C: Refuse to immunize the child until the parent stops asking questions
options.D: Listen patiently and explain the true benefits and safety of the vaccine

explanation: Great nurses never judge or brush off patient fears. Listening with empathy and sharing accurate facts builds strong trust! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h6)

question: When is a formative evaluation done during an IEC program?

options.A: While nurses are writing hospital financial reports
options.B: Before the program starts, to test messages and materials
options.C: As an emergency response to a sudden disease outbreak
options.D: Only after all health campaigns have permanently ended

explanation: Think of formative evaluation as 'forming' your plan—you test your posters and messages before launching to make sure they actually make sense to the community. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h7)

question: What is the main goal of a summative evaluation at the end of an IEC campaign?

options.A: To measure the final impact and changes in community health behavior
options.B: To replace traditional rulers with modern local government staff
options.C: To check if the printing budget was spent on the exact correct date
options.D: To decide which nurse should be transferred to another clinic

explanation: Summative evaluation happens at the 'summary' or end of the project to check: did our campaign actually work? Did health habits improve? [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h7)

question: Which of these is NOT a common barrier to health behavior change in primary care?

options.A: High rates of illiteracy among the target audience
options.B: Extreme poverty and lack of basic financial resources
options.C: Deep-seated cultural norms and traditional beliefs
options.D: Guaranteed financial wealth for every household

explanation: Poverty, illiteracy, and strong cultural traditions can make health changes tough, but having guaranteed wealth certainly wouldn't be a barrier! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h8)

question: If a community has high rates of illiteracy, how should nurses adjust their health education strategy?

options.A: Only people who went to secondary school are allowed to visit the clinic
options.B: Nurses must rely more on verbal talks, drama, and pictures than written pamphlets
options.C: Written textbooks become the primary method of teaching villagers
options.D: Health education must be completely cancelled until everyone learns to read

explanation: When people cannot read written text easily, visual aids, storytelling, local drama, and spoken words are wonderful ways to get the health message across! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T9#GNS124_U5_T9_h8)
